messages:
Ria Desai: Heads-up: a new hire hit a weird failure on Windows when following the quickstart. They copied the PowerShell example verbatim and got `Invalid API key`/401.

Omar Khan: PowerShell vs Bash quoting is always a trap. What does the README show?

Ria Desai: It shows: `set REDWOOD_API_KEY=abcd1234` (which is a Windows CMD form) and also a PowerShell example below that uses single quotes around the header: `-H 'Authorization: Bearer $env:REDWOOD_API_KEY'`. That combination breaks for PowerShell and for users on cmd.

Samir Gupta: Yikes. So docs mix CMD, PowerShell, and Bash idioms. New users copy the wrong snippet and get 401/403.

Omar Khan: Can repro: PowerShell wants `setx` for persistent env or `$env:REDWOOD_API_KEY = '...'` for session. And headers need double quotes or escaped vars for Invoke-RestMethod. The current curl line with single quotes won't expand vars in PowerShell.

Ria Desai: Also saw a Windows PowerShell example that used backticks for multiline and then copy/paste loses backslashes — super confusing. We should make each shell explicit and test them in CI.

Samir Gupta: Agreed. Proposed changes: 1) standardize on `REDWOOD_API_KEY` across all examples; 2) provide three clear env examples: mac/Linux (export), Windows CMD (setx or set), PowerShell ($env:); 3) provide curl header examples for each shell showing correct quoting/expansion; 4) small troubleshooting note: 401 -> check env var method, 403 -> check token scope.

Ria Desai: I'll draft the snippets and open a PR. For PowerShell we should show both Invoke-RestMethod and curl (Windows curl maps to curl.exe vs alias). Example: `curl.exe -H "Authorization: Bearer $env:REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'` and `Invoke-RestMethod -Headers @{ Authorization = "Bearer $env:REDWOOD_API_KEY" } -Uri https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -Method Post -Body (ConvertTo-Json @{ prompt = "hi" })`.

Omar Khan: Nice. Also add a tiny callout about GitHub Codespaces / devcontainers where env var propagation differs. New hires often run into that when following the quickstart in an editor terminal.

Samir Gupta: And add a CI smoke test that runs the README curl examples in bash and PowerShell (use native curl.exe on Windows in the runner) with a dummy key to validate formatting/expansion, so we catch regressions.

Ria Desai: Draft pushed: https://git.redwood/docs/pull/4012 includes: explicit shell examples (bash, cmd, powershell), curl.exe PowerShell note, env var parity, troubleshooting section, and CI smoke test. Requesting docs review.

docs-bot: docs-bot: Label `DX` added, requested reviewers: @omar, @samir.

Omar Khan: Reviewed, left one nit about wording in the PowerShell Invoke-RestMethod example.

Samir Gupta: Approved.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: docs site updated: https://docs.redwood.ai/quickstart version 2026-03-25T09:12Z :rocket:

Ria Desai: Closing thread. I'll run a short grep across sample apps to ensure env var parity and shell examples are consistent. Thanks!
